                                                                    Abstract

                                         Despite the significant success of imitation learning in
                                         robotic manipulation, its application to bimanual tasks
                                         remains highly challenging. Existing approaches mainly
                                         learn a policy to predict a distant next-best end-effector
                                         pose (NBP) and then compute the corresponding joint rota-
                                         tion angles for motion using inverse kinematics. However,
                                                                                                                                       Self-Collision
                                         they suffer from two important issues: (1) rarely consider-
                                         ing the physical robotic structure, which may cause self-
                                         collisions or interferences, and (2) overlooking the kine-            Figure 1. The self-collision problem in bimanual manipulation
                                         matics constraint, which may result in the predicted poses            tasks due to overlooking the robotic structure.
                                         not conforming to the actual limitations of the robot joints.
                                         In this paper, we propose Kinematics enhanced Spatial-                plex tasks requiring two-arm coordination. While imitation
                                         TemporAl gRaph Diffuser (KStar Diffuser). Specifically,               learning has demonstrated remarkable success in single-arm
                                         (1) to incorporate the physical robot structure information           manipulation [6, 7, 34, 37? ], its extension to bimanual
                                         into action prediction, KStar Diffuser maintains a dynamic            scenarios faces unique challenges as robots need to coor-
                                         spatial-temporal graph according to the physical bimanual             dinate dual-arm movements while conforming to physical
                                         joint motions at continuous timesteps. This dynamic graph             constraints. These challenges significantly impact the reli-
                                         serves as the robot-structure condition for denoising the ac-         ability and feasibility of predicted actions in real-world ap-
                                         tions; (2) to make the NBP learning objective consistent              plications.
                                         with kinematics, we introduce the differentiable kinematics               A straightforward approach [9, 10, 13, 60, 61, 65] would
                                         to provide the reference for optimizing KStar Diffuser. This          be to learn the entire motion trajectory by predicting joint
                                         module regularizes the policy to predict more reliable and            positions at consecutive timesteps. However, this poses sig-
                                         kinematics-aware next end-effector poses. Experimental re-            nificant challenges as trajectories are typically long and dif-
                                         sults show that our method effectively leverages the physi-           ficult to learn. Therefore, mainstream approaches [15, 17,
                                         cal structural information and generates kinematics-aware             35, 49] typically adopt a two-stage pipeline: first predict-
                                         actions in both simulation and real-world.                            ing the next-best end-effector pose (NBP), then computing

Figure 2. Overview of KStar Diffuser. The top part presents the spatial-temporal graph which is constructed according to the robot
architecture. The bottom part shows our backbone and the proposed kinematics regularizer. For the backbone, it extracts the multimodal
information which consists of multiview RGB-D observations and language instruction, and then generates bimanual 6D end-effector
poses. The kinematics regularizer enhances pose learning by incorporating joint-level predictions, which are mapped to reference end-
effector poses through differentiable forward kinematics (FK).

D. Qualitative Analysis
We show more qualitative result in Figure D. Through the
novel approach of encoding robotic arm structural infor-
mation as graph representations and explicitly incorporat-
ing kinematic constraints, our model demonstrates excep-
tional performance in motion symmetry, synchronization,
and coordination across dual-arm manipulation tasks. In the
lift ball experiment, the model achieves precise bilat-
eral symmetry in spatial positioning through learned struc-
tured representations. The dual arms maintain stable sym-
metric configurations while preventing object instability
through synchronized force application patterns, highlight-
ing the efficacy of our structure-aware control paradigm.
Furthermore, in the push box task, the model exhibits re-
markable geometric symmetry in motion planning and ex-
ecution. By leveraging embedded kinematic information,
the robotic arms consistently maintain equidistant position-
ing relative to the target object’s center of mass while exe-
cuting synchronized trajectories along parallel paths. This
precise symmetrical control not only ensures operational
stability during object manipulation but also establishes a
robust framework for dual-arm cooperative control in com-
plex manipulation scenarios.
